budget_note: E1's two arms share one update count, so the expanded arm sees each of its samples fewer times: a fixed-compute data-scale contrast, not an equal-epoch one. The LONG arm instead gives the expanded split the same six exposures, with the cosine horizon set to its own total from step one. Comparing LONG with the short expanded run is therefore a schedule-and-budget comparison, not the causal effect of exposure count alone.
checkpoint_selection: lowest V0 official_d3 among planned eval steps; ties go to the earlier step

interval_length_auxiliary.added_to: the existing total loss; the D3 and auxiliary weights are unchanged
interval_length_auxiliary.loss: sum_n complete[n] * sum_k |ell_pred - ell_gt| / (6 * plan_complete), with plan_complete the same full-effective-batch denominator the D3 loss uses
interval_length_auxiliary.never_replaces_d3: an interval norm carries no direction, so a mirrored path scores identically under this term alone

adjacent_edges.changed: the three adjacent-past comparisons become readable
adjacent_edges.control: MR-ADJ0 (the same module, the three new edges masked out)
adjacent_edges.endpoint_encoding: [age_ref, age_src, dt, log dt] instead of [dt, log dt], applied identically in both arms, because dt alone cannot separate (0,-0.1) from (-0.1,-0.2) nor (0,-0.5) from (-0.5,-1.0)
adjacent_edges.masked_softmax_safety: star edges are never masked, so no query sees an all-masked memory
adjacent_edges.new_observations: none: the same five images are read; only the number of relations computed between them changes
adjacent_edges.output_projection_init: zeros, so step zero reproduces MR exactly
adjacent_edges.pair_convention: (reference, source); the source is the older frame, matching local_correlation's argument order
adjacent_edges.readouts: history still reads the four star edges and keeps its four existing targets; state and the planner consume the residual-updated motion feature
adjacent_edges.star_path: preserved bit for bit; the module contributes a residual

matching_resolution.lowdetail_recipe: 768 -> 384 -> 768 with PIL bilinear, inside the loader's own resize step, before jitter and normalisation
matching_resolution.scene_branch: untouched: its own backbone pass on the original 384x216 stack
matching_resolution.unchanged_reach: radius 4 on the 768x432 canvas reproduces the original fine +/-32 and coarse +/-64 original-image pixels, so only the quantisation changes, not the reach
